 New Japanese pair shock Pearly-Thinaah in first round of Japan Masters
 New Japanese pair shock Pearly-Thinaah in first round of Japan Masters
 10-Nov-2026, 18:16 10 Nov 2026, 18:16 K. Parkaran Share The world No 4 Malaysian pair were defeated by 214th-ranked Ririna Hiramoto-Chiharu Shida, who are competing in only their third tournament as partners.
 Pearly Tan-M Thinaah lost 21-18, 13-21, 14-21 to Ririna Hiramoto-Chiharu Shida in 64 minutes. (Bernama pic) 
 PETALING JAYA : World No 4 women’s doubles pair Pearly Tan-M Thinaah crashed out of the Japan Masters in the opening round, losing to 214th-ranked Japanese pair Ririna Hiramoto-Chiharu Shida in three games. 
 In a match marred by numerous unforced errors, the tournament’s second seeds lost 21-18, 13-21, 14-21 in 64 minutes at the World Tour Super 500 championship held at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium.
 It was a major upset as Ririna-Chiharu only started playing together last month, and this was their third tournament as partners. However, the experienced Chiharu has won several major titles with other partners.
 Pearly-Thinaah won their second World Tour title this year at the Denmark Open last month after winning the Indonesia Masters in January.
 Despite this loss, the Malaysian pair are well positioned to qualify for the prestigious World Tour Finals, to be held in Hangzhou, China, from Dec 9-13, as they currently lead the qualification standings.
 Only the top eight in the various categories will be selected, with a maximum of two per country.
